rows.answer: Under standard claim timelines, you have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a main reimbursement claim [2] (archived 2024 rules state 15 days [1]), whereas under group corporate plans, the deadline is 60 days from discharge [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months for retail plans, declared pre-existing conditions, and the Hospital Cash Benefit plan [2][4][5], but is reduced to 24 months under the Aurora Senior Care plan [2].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days [1][2].
Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals as of 1 April 2026 [1].

The no-claim bonus on the Gold plan is 25% of the base sum insured per claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100%, and it stops accumulating for that year rather than being reduced if a claim is made [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment because infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Aurora Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If Aurora's Stage 1 response is unsatisfactory, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) [1]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you may escalate to the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [3].
Ambulance cover is ₹5,000 per hospitalisation, for road ambulance only [1][3][5].
Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, subject to a 30-day initial waiting period [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned or cancelled for a refund [2][5], which is 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days for policies sold through distance marketing [1][2].
You get 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances and is payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement, excluding out-patient treatment [2].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a TPA [1].
To qualify as a hospital, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, not everything will be paid [1][2]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% (₹10,000 per day) [1][2]. Because the room cost of ₹15,000 per day exceeds this limit, proportionate deduction applies, reducing the payout for the room rent and all associated hospital charges proportionately and requiring out-of-pocket payment [1][2].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, but not under Bronze [2]. 

When adding a 63-year-old parent, the policy premium is determined by the age of the eldest covered member [3], and if on the Silver plan, a 10% co-payment will apply to every claim because the eldest insured member is over 60 [4].

Your served waiting period will carry over only up to the sum insured of your previous policy (including accrued no-claim bonus), while any increased or excess sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount [1][2].

To continue coverage for your baby beyond 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the newborn to your policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [1]. Doing so within this 90-day window ensures guaranteed-issue addition without medical underwriting [1].

Under the Bronze plan, out-patient consultations, diagnostics, and pharmacy are not covered under the base plan, and the optional OPD rider is not available [1]. The provided sources do not specifically mention out-patient physiotherapy, so whether it can be reimbursed cannot be fully determined from the sources.
A claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points; it does not reset it to zero [1].

On the Gold plan, the maternity coverage limit for a caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1] and proportionate deduction does not apply [2], leaving you with an out-of-pocket cost of ₹60,000 on a bill of ₹1,60,000 [1][2].
No, knee replacement is not covered immediately and is subject to a 24-month waiting period, unless it is required following an accident, which is covered from day one [2][3].

Total discounts are capped at 30% of the base premium, with the wellness discount (which provides up to an additional 15% at renewal) applied last after the cap as the only discount that may exceed it [1][4].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider [2]. Your only option is reimbursement with pre-approval, which is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [2].
You have 45 days from the date of the query to respond for standard reimbursement claims [1], or 30 days from the date of the query for motor insurance claims [4].
A planned cashless admission must be notified at least 72 hours before admission [2][3], although archived 2024 rules state 48 hours before admission [1].
Aurora settles a reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2].
The Aurora Gold plan has no co-payment at all ages [1], and the Aurora Silver plan has no co-payment when the eldest insured member is below age 60 [2].

The pre- and post-hospitalisation cover windows across the four plans are:
- **Bronze:** 30 days pre-hospitalisation and 60 days post-hospitalisation [1].
- **Silver:** 45 days pre-hospitalisation and 90 days post-hospitalisation [1].
- **Gold:** 60 days pre-hospitalisation and 120 days post-hospitalisation [1].
- **Platinum:** 90 days pre-hospitalisation and 180 days post-hospitalisation [1].
You should buy the Gold plan or Platinum plan, as Gold removes room-rent sub-limits [2] and both the Gold and Platinum plans cover dependent parents-in-law [5].
Dental treatment and oral surgery are excluded, unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2][3]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is not covered by any plan [1].

For health insurance policies, you lose your accumulated no-claim bonus and waiting periods restart if you do not pay before the grace period expires, which is 30 days from the renewal due date for annual policies and 15 days for policies paid in instalments [1].

No, a denial of cashless is not a rejection of the claim [1]. Depending on the reason for denial (such as insufficient information regarding medical necessity or an unexpired waiting period), you can pay the hospital directly and file for reimbursement [1].

Completing the quit-tobacco programme earns 200 wellness points, which contribute toward a renewal-premium discount (1,000 points = 5% discount, capped at 15%) [1][5]. However, the provided sources do not specify whether or how points earned by a parent apply directly to you individually [1][2].
The sum insured options for AUR-HI-SIL-2026 are ₹5,00,000 or ₹10,00,000 [1][2].
No, refractive error correction is permanently excluded where the error is less than 7.5 dioptres [1].
